s2.ptxt: Application Temperature

s3.ptxt: When the ambient temperature is low (15°C or less), use an infrared lamp to warm the base (body application surface) and blackout tape to 20-30°C before performing the work. Also, when the temperature is high (35°C or more), cool them to 35°C or less before performing the work.

item.ptxt: The suitable temperature for applying blackout tape is 25°C.
At low temperatures, adhesion is weak and the blackout tape is hard and tends to lift. Also, at high temperatures, the blackout tape loses its stiffness.

s2.ptxt: Work Before Application

s3.ptxt: If paint nibs, dust, etc. adhere to the base (body application surface), air will be trapped when the blackout tape is pressed on, causing poor appearance; therefore, remove paint nibs and also remove dust from the base, the area around the base and the blackout tape.

atten4.ptxt: Since it is dry in winter, sandwich the blackout tape between pieces of cardboard, etc. and store it in a dry, flat place.

s2.ptxt: Handling Blackout Tape

s3.ptxt: Blackout tape deforms easily, so sandwich it between pieces of cardboard, etc. and store it in a dry, flat place.

atten3.ptxt: Do not bend it or leave it in a hot place.

s2.ptxt: Tips for Applying Blackout Tape (Squeegee Operation and Application Method - General Areas)

item.ptxt: Positioning at the start of application affects appearance and peeling, so perform it with an accuracy of ±1mm.
Once blackout tape has been peeled off, it deforms and its adhesive strength drops, so it cannot be reused.

s3.ptxt: To prevent air bubbles, lightly lift the part not being pressed by the squeegee so that it does not contact the base, tilt the squeegee at 40-50° (push direction) or 30-45° (pull direction), and press the tape on by pushing air outward at a slow, constant speed of 3-7cm/second with a pressing force of 20-30N{2-3kgf}.

atten3.ptxt: If the squeegee speed is changed during the operation, the squeegee is stopped, or the pressing force changes, streaks (horizontal streaks called shock lines) may appear on the surface of the blackout tape, and if the speed is too fast, air bubbles may be trapped; therefore, pay attention to keeping the speed, pressing force and squeegee operating angle constant when performing the work.

item.ptxt: The squeegee may be tilted in either the push direction or the pull direction depending on the application area.
Perform the work while peeling off the release paper of the blackout tape 10-20mm ahead of the tip of the squeegee.

s2.ptxt: Tips for Applying Blackout Tape (Squeegee Operation and Application Method - Hemmed Areas)

s3.ptxt: For areas that cannot be pressed with the squeegee at one time, press them on in several steps. In particular, for small radii at hemmed areas, gradually adhere the tape in 2-3 steps using your finger or the thick end of the squeegee.

atten4.ptxt: For the back side of hemmed areas, after peeling off the release paper, adhere the tape using your finger or the thick end of the squeegee.

s2.ptxt: Tips for Applying Blackout Tape (Squeegee Operation and Application Method - Corners)

s3.ptxt: At corners, after peeling off the release paper, carefully adhere the tape with your fingertips.
To prevent poor appearance due to sharp tape corners, heat the blackout tape with a dryer before folding in each corner, and then fold in and adhere the corners in order.

s2.ptxt: Inspection After Application

s3.ptxt: If poor appearance occurs after application is complete, reapply using new blackout tape.

item.ptxt: Do not peel off and reapply the blackout tape.
Scratches are noticeable on glossy items such as tape applied to outer panels, so do not use a needle to fix air bubbles.

atten4.ptxt: If the hemmed areas or corners of the blackout tape are slightly peeled off, repair them with instant adhesive.

s2.ptxt: Clean Adhesive Surface (When Using Infrared Lamp)

s3.ptxt: Warm the blackout tape and adhesive remaining on the body with an infrared lamp.

atten3.ptxt: Be careful of burns from the heated body or the heat of the infrared lamp.

s3.ptxt: Using a shop rag, etc., scrape off the blackout tape and adhesive remaining on the body.
Clean the adhesive surface with white gasoline.

s2.ptxt: Clean Adhesive Surface (When Using Tape Removal Disc)

s3.ptxt: Set 8 discs in the holder, and install the removal disc to an air drill or electric drill.

atten3.ptxt: Use an electric drill with a no-load speed of 2000-3000r/min.

s3.ptxt: Using the removal disc, scrape off the blackout tape and adhesive remaining on the body.

item.ptxt: Wear protective glasses when performing the work.
Pay attention to the disc rotation direction and work progress direction.
To avoid damaging the body by scraping too much, visually check the area being scraped while working.

s3.ptxt: Clean the bonding surface with white gasoline.
